title: One Of The Better Things That Ever Has Happened

contact_edits.before: Weidman's script doesn't overstress the story's resonance as a representative American fable, but it's inescapably there, especially now. Sondheim's score, as intelligent and exploratory as expected, combines jagged with jaunty; it also includes a bewitching long-lined ballad (The Best Thing That Ever Has Happened) unlike anything in his previous work. But he hasn't got as deeply inside his characters as usual. It's far more Addison's show than it's Wilson's -- the opening number is about him -- but in the end, we don't know whether he's his brother's victim or the architect (sorry) of his own misfortune. If it is both, the proportions aren't clear. I doubt, though, that this is the end of the road for Road Show. There's too much gold there, too much bounce, for some theatre not to try it again. - Road Show is at the Public Theater in New York City until Dec. 28. Call 212-967-7555 for tickets and information.
